exactGap: Decks are already producible two ways: the model writes python-pptx inside code_interpreter (advertised at tool_loop.rs:4320, python-pptx 1.0.2 baked into the execution-core image) and the browser turns one answer into a PPTX (chat-export/pptx.ts planSlides, one slide per level-1/2 heading with a bullet and character budget). What does not exist is any tool-owned deck manifest or per-slide state, any render or validation step (the sandbox image installs no renderer such as LibreOffice and the per-call workspace is deleted when the call returns), a slide strip or present mode (no hits in the frontend or Model Plane), and any template or brand-token skill kind (AgentSkill is text content plus triggers and tool restrictions only). Plan H8 (research report to designed PPTX, Wave 5, depends on H4 native charts) is the planned seed and OD18 recommends a neutral theme with a DeckTheme seam, but H8 has no manifest, validation gate, present mode or template library.
reuse: code_interpreter (python-pptx, matplotlib PNG charts, files_in staging up to 8 MiB per file and 16 MiB total, generated files returned as download cards)

durable Space workspace design (workspace_hydrate.rs, sandbox.rs extra_ro_binds read-only layers) for mounting template files into the sandbox; hydrate is still standalone per its own header
artifacts pipeline (ArtifactKind::File) for delivery; plan items H4 (native charts) and H8 (deck path v1)
constraints: The sandbox is MpNetworkPolicy::Disabled with a ~30 s timeout and a workspace deleted after every call, so the manifest must be owned by the tool or gateway (not the sandbox) and brand templates must be staged through files_in or read-only workspace layers, never fetched. Under ZDR the gateway does not seed or persist artifacts (sse.rs:4047-4057), so a durable manifest and org template library must be refused or kept client-session-only for ZDR threads. Brand and template files are org or Space content owned by Data Plane (document is the only ownable resource type in user-core's taxonomy), and Space access never widens that ACL. The per-slide render gate depends on a renderer that does not exist in the sandbox image (F-t3-014), which adds image size and attack surface.
approachAdjustment: Do not frame it as a new slides tool family on top of nothing: first deliver plan H4/H8 on the existing code_interpreter path, then add the manifest as a small validated JSON schema that a deck-build helper renders with python-pptx, and have the SPA draw the slide strip and present mode from the manifest JSON rather than from the PPTX. Make per-slide validation structural (shape bounds, overflow heuristics, notes present) unless F-t3-014 lands a real renderer. Ship templates as org-authored skills first and brand tokens through the DeckTheme seam, which is what OD18 and OD19 ('templates are user-authored first') already recommend; the reference file and preview parts of a template skill need Data Plane storage, not the agent_skills text column.
effortNote: Kept at L on the assumption that the F-t3-014 render step and plan H4 charts land separately; without a renderer the validation gate is structural only, and adding a renderer to the sandbox image would push this to XL.
verdictReason: Not shipped, but the item's premise that only a browser-side export exists is wrong (code_interpreter python-pptx is advertised and baked into the image) and plan H8 already plans the base deck path; the real delta is manifest, validation gate, present mode and template library, so the recommendation should be rewritten as that delta on top of H8.

Replay primitives exist (session-core ReplayThread, gateway GET /v1/threads/:id/events and /v1/runs/:id/events/replay) but are envelope-only or browser-agent projections by deliberate design, so a content-bearing replay needs a new redacted projection, and there is no ForkThread RPC (artifacts.rs fork_thread only forks artifact counters) and no 'import' value in session-core THREAD_ORIGINS. Export is partly shipped (per-answer Word, Excel, PowerPoint and print-to-PDF built in the browser via ChatMessages.tsx exportMenuItems) but there is no whole-conversation export (the DSAR export is Control-Plane-only by its own disclosure) and no ChatGPT or Claude importer.

constraints: Threads are owned by session-core, so the snapshot entity belongs in Model Plane, but grants and admin policy must be Control Plane authority: add a new resource type to user-core's resource_taxonomy.json (the Go embed, the retrieval-engine-rs mirror and the lint script must stay in parity) rather than any Model Plane-local ACL; Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. Build the share as an immutable redacted snapshot copy (OD19 recommends an org-internal sign-in link, 30-day expiry, revocable, redacted text view) rather than a live view of the thread, and do not describe replay as 'built from the durable run event log' because that log is envelope-only today. effortNote: Bundles a snapshot entity with Control grants and redaction, a new redacted replay projection, whole-conversation export, an importer and a fork dependency. Recommend splitting: share snapshot L (owner-gated by OD19, plan Wave 6 says do not start), export M, import M.
verdictReason: Share is correctly missing but already planned and owner-gated (I19), the replay premise is wrong as stated (event logs are envelope-only by design), ForkThread does not exist, and export is partly shipped; the item should be split and its dependencies corrected.

exactGap: The gateway already owns the artifact version counter and current text (artifacts.rs ArtifactVersionStore, process-local and rehydrated from each assistant turn's metadata.artifacts by sse.rs rehydrate_persisted_artifacts) and serialises run-versus-run commits with lock_commit and unchanged_from, but there is no artifact store with its own revision ids, no HTTP route to read, write or restore an artifact, no editor attribution, and ZDR turns are not persisted at all. The panel (ChatArtifactPanel.tsx) has a read-only version stepper built from client-merged history (chat-artifacts.ts mergeArtifactVersion), a diff, copy and browser-side export, but no edit, restore or selection capability (no getSelection or selectionchange anywhere in verevonv3/src). Annotation overlay and collaborative documents are absent: Application Plane has only plannerDocuments metadata and presence, and no yrs or yjs dependency was found in any Cargo.toml, package.json or go.mod.
reuse: ArtifactVersionStore (counter, content, kind, title index) and its per-thread commit lock plus base-comparison guard (lock_commit, unchanged_from) as the concurrency model for a user save
sse.rs rehydrate_persisted_artifacts and metadata.artifacts as the existing durable representation of versions
revision_preservation.rs section parser (byte-for-byte preservation of untouched Markdown sections) for selection or section scoped rewrites
update_artifact and read_artifact tools for the model-side revision path
ChatArtifactPanel version stepper and diffText, chat-artifacts.ts mergeArtifactVersion
POST /v1/chat/documents (create_document) as the existing path to promote text into Data Plane for save to knowledge

constraints: Under effective ZDR the gateway neither seeds nor persists artifacts (sse.rs:4047-4057), so a durable version store, restore or collaboration cannot exist for ZDR threads and editing there must stay client-session-only. Artifact content lives in session-core thread metadata (Model Plane owns it); save to knowledge must go through Data Plane document creation with the user's delegated token so owner=user, not a second copy of storage. Application Plane realtime projections must not become the source of truth for owner-plane content, and an AI edit inside a shared document needs an explicit whose-authority decision. OD19 ruled that selection edits stay at phase 1 and I18 (a server range patch) is cut, so Phase 1 must not introduce a server range-patch API.
approachAdjustment: Rewrite Phase 1 as plan I17: client-side highlight-to-edit through the normal model revision path and restore this version by re-emitting an old revision as a new version. Drop the 'expected revision plus lock while a run targets the same artifact' server design from Phase 1; the gateway already has a per-thread commit lock and base comparison for run races, so a later user-save RPC should go through the same lock_commit/unchanged_from path and append a new version with an editor attribute. Treat Phase 2 (annotation) and Phase 3 (yrs collaborative documents) as separate, later bets: Phase 3 duplicates ground Data Plane and Application Plane would own.
effortNote: XL stands only for all three phases together. Phase 1 alone is M (plan I17, about a week); Phase 2 annotation M; Phase 3 collaborative documents XL.
verdictReason: Phase 1 is already planned (I17, Wave 5) and the item mis-states the baseline (the gateway already owns counter, content and a run concurrency guard; only the history assembly is client-side); Phases 2 and 3 are genuinely absent and should be separated.

exactGap: Register, share, delete, OAuth start/callback and a one-call connect exist, and connect already auto-discovers tools/list and allows every tool when no allowlist is given (http_routes.rs resolve_tool_allowlist), but there is no probe endpoint that returns tools and auth requirements without saving, no tool picker (McpServersSection takes a typed allowlist) and no test call. Static bearer or API-key MCP servers cannot be registered at all because validate_mcp_server rejects any raw token (only OAuth tokens, vaulted in capability-core, work), and there is no REST/API-key connector kind (integration-corev2's catalogue is OAuth-dominant). The sandbox side has only a seam: MpNetworkPolicy::AllowDomains plus a fail-closed check for HTTPS_PROXY, but code_interpreter forces Disabled, no egress proxy service exists, and AllowDomains keeps the host network rather than a proxy-only namespace.
reuse: McpHttpSession::connect and list_tools (http_list_tools) as the probe core, and mcp_oauth discover_protected_resource for auth detection
safe_mcp_http_client, endpoint_host_is_forbidden and ip_is_forbidden (DNS-resolved, IP-pinned SSRF guard) in runtime_registries.rs

constraints: Ingestion Plane (integration-corev2) owns provider actions and outbound HTTP to third parties, so the REST/API connector executor and egress proxy belong there (reusing its SSRF client, allowlist and vault) with capability-core holding only the catalogue entry; the Model proposes and the executor enforces host allow-lists and injects secrets. Raw secrets must never sit in the Model Plane registry (validate_mcp_server rejects them on purpose): use vault-resolved secret references. ZDR: registration is a durable mutation refused under ZDR (require_non_zdr_durable_mutation), and integration-corev2 classes unassessed api_key providers as cannot_verify, so custom connectors must be unavailable in ZDR threads unless attested. Org-scope sharing stays inside the owner ACL (Scope::Org needs an admin claim; Space access never widens it). Proxy and probe must keep the same SSRF and DNS-pinning guards and keep secrets out of logs and traces.
approachAdjustment: Put the REST/API connector executor and egress proxy in integration-corev2 (or reuse its egress client) instead of a new Model Plane egress service. Implement the probe as a thin wrapper over http_list_tools and discover_protected_resource that returns the tool list and auth requirement without persisting. Fix the static-token path with a secret-reference registration step: today McpServersSection sends the token field and validate_mcp_server rejects it. Split the sandbox proxy-only namespace into its own optional item: AllowDomains as built is advisory (host network kept, proxy via environment variable) and needs a real proxy-only network namespace before it enforces anything.
effortNote: L holds for probe, tool picker, secret-reference MCP auth and the REST connector in integration-corev2; the proxy-only sandbox namespace is a separate L and should be split out or demoted.
verdictReason: Partial: the probe primitives and SSRF guards already exist and connect auto-discovers tools, but the item misses that static-token MCP is rejected today and places the proxy in a Model Plane service when Ingestion owns provider egress and vaulting; split the sandbox part out.

exactGap: What exists: drain.rs (graceful shutdown on redeploy only), a user pause (PauseRun/ResumeRun, an in-memory RunStatus::Paused honoured only by the browser-agent loop), a durable HITL pause (agent.rs pause_for_approval creates a session-core approval with a continuation descriptor and sets AwaitingApproval) whose cold resume through approval_delivery_worker.rs covers only three idempotent action kinds, admission-time budget checks (org_quota.rs reads org-core ceilings and fails open on an org-core outage, then cost-core check_budget returns a hard 402 budget_exceeded; no mid-run cost check was found), and per-turn model, effort (quick|standard|deep mapped server-side to a clamped thinking budget) and approval posture that a client can only tighten. What is missing: any org-level or global agent pause (searches for org pause, kill switch and emergency stop found only per-feature env switches), a paused_for_credit status and any loop-level cold resume (run status strings are queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled, awaiting_approval, and the worker's own header calls resuming a live loop a larger problem it does not attempt), and a typed per-turn override envelope clamped against Control entitlements (no entitlement clamp on the requested model was found).
reuse: durable HITL pause: agent.rs pause_for_approval (session-core CreateApproval with continuation descriptor, AwaitingApproval), ResumeRun with validate_granted_approval, and approval_delivery_worker.rs as the pattern for a credit-wait pause that a billing event can grant

drain.rs as the model for in-flight completion semantics
constraints: Control Plane owns entitlements and org policy, so the pause flag must be a Control-side org setting with Model Plane only reading it at admission and at each continuation; the Control-decision path for effectful and scheduled steps is the natural fail-closed enforcement point, while org_quota's fail-open-on-outage behaviour is wrong for a kill switch and needs an explicit documented policy. Execution-core has no database, so a durable paused_for_credit state must be recorded through session-core (system of record, as approvals are today), and it is not possible for ZDR runs, which are persistence-free (run_control is refused for them): those must end with a clear failure rather than persist state. Overrides must be validated server-side and may only restrict or select within Control entitlements, never widen approval posture or ZDR.
approachAdjustment: Split into three pieces. (1) The org pause switch first: a Control org setting enforced in the gateway admission path next to org_quota, in Control's per-step decision issuance for effects and scheduled steps, and as a gate in the agent loop (only browser_agent polls Paused today). (2) A typed per-turn override envelope reusing the existing effort, posture and model fields with an entitlement clamp. (3) paused_for_credit last: a durable HITL pause exists, but cold resume only re-executes three idempotent action kinds and its own header says resuming a live loop is a larger problem, so a credit pause needs a round-boundary pause that a billing event can grant and a proven re-entry of run_agent from the durable transcript; the item's 'cheap once runs are resumable' premise is only partly true.
effortNote: Raised from M. The org pause switch alone is M and overrides are S to M, but paused_for_credit needs a new approval kind, a billing-event resume trigger and loop-level re-entry that the delivery worker does not provide, which is L and depends on durable run continuation (F-t3-002).
verdictReason: The three asks are genuinely missing, but the item understates what exists (PauseRun/Paused, the durable approval pause, the admission budget check, clamped effort and posture) and misjudges the cost of paused_for_credit; split it and lead with the org pause switch.

exactGap: Per-org entitlements already exist in Control Plane (org-core org_entitlements table seeded with default feature.* keys, GET /organizations/:id/entitlements, proxied by the gateway and read by the SPA for the ZDR entitlement check) and billing-core keeps per-account feature_flags and entitlements that its feature check evaluates, but there is no typed registry (stage, owner, kill switch, agentAccess), no operator or admin write route for entitlements, and Model Plane services read none of it (org_quota.rs reads org-core quotas only; Go services use Control-signed decisions that carry an entitlement revision). Model Plane features are gated by independent per-service env vars (AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_ENABLED, FINETUNE_ENABLED, LEARNING_RUN_EVENTS_ENABLED, PROMOTE_ON_USE_ENABLED and others) plus a promotion-ledger TSV, so changing one means a redeploy. The model-executable action allowlist (model-eligibility.ts) already acts as an agent-access gate and currently excludes every settings action.
reuse: org-core org_entitlements (per-org key and enabled), its GET route, the gateway /api/v1/orgs/{id}/entitlements proxy and the SPA organization-client
billing-core Account.Entitlements / FeatureFlags and the plan-driven refresh as the entitlement seed
org_quota.rs (service-token derivation per org, call pattern into org-core) as the template for a Model Plane flag client; its fail-open outage behaviour must not be copied for security gates
Control-signed decisions (ResolveRunActionAuthority, ResolveScheduledStepAuthority) that already re-resolve entitlement before an effect

CAPABILITY_PROMOTION_LEDGER.tsv as the evidence record to link flags to
constraints: Control Plane owns entitlements, quotas and billing, so extend org-core's entitlement store (billing-core stays the plan-driven seed) rather than create a second Control registry; registry definitions may live in mp-contracts but evaluation is per org through Control Plane with a TTL cache that fails closed for security gates. A flag may only restrict: it must never widen ZDR or authority posture. Some env switches are deployment-ordering gates (AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_ENABLED is turned on only after the new execution-core is the one running, and its module states a deployed process never changes its environment), so those must stay env, not become runtime per-org flags. Nothing may expose a settings write action to the model until agentAccess exists.
approachAdjustment: Start from org-core entitlements: add an operator/admin write route and stage/owner metadata, then add a small Model Plane client modelled on org_quota.rs with a TTL cache, and migrate only flags with a real per-org use (hooks, MCP dispatch, Do-on-subscription staging, fine-tuning). Leave deployment-ordering env switches alone. Map agentAccess onto the existing action-registry and model-eligibility allowlist instead of a new concept, and serve the SPA subset through the entitlements endpoint the gateway already proxies (the SPA reads it today only for the ZDR entitlement check in organization-client.ts) rather than a new boot payload.
effortNote: Unchanged. Storage, read route, gateway proxy and SPA client already exist; the cost is the write path, the schema crate and a cached Model Plane client.
verdictReason: The claim of no per-org evaluation and no Control-side flag store is wrong for Control Plane and the SPA (org entitlements and plan feature flags exist) and right for Model Plane; reword as extending org-core entitlements, keeping deployment-ordering switches as env.

exactGap: (a) promote_on_use.rs (maybe_promote, called from runtime_loop/mod.rs:786 only for web_fetch and Quarry web-read results in the execution-core agent loop, never from the chat-loop fetch_url) is a complete no-op unless PROMOTE_ON_USE_ENABLED, dry-run unless PROMOTE_ON_USE_EXECUTE, keeps a process-local counter, counts successful fetches rather than citations, and promotes through Quarry /v1/scrape with a service token so the document would be owned by the service principal; no Model Plane deploy or config file searched sets it. It also passes no ZDR flag, and Quarry ignores a service token's ZDR floor and trusts the body flag, so an armed promote would durably ingest pages fetched in a ZDR run, a blocker the module's own two listed refinements do not mention. (b) The Norwegian data tools carry only prose guidance in tool_loop.rs descriptions (get_weather covers 10 cities, get_statistics covers population only), the capability registry already has a coarse cost_class and seeded org skills steer tool choice, but no use_when or cost_hint field exists.
reuse: Quarry /v1/scrape ingest primitive (owner from signed claims, ZDR from the body flag, durable crawl and batch jobs refused under ZDR) and execution-core quarry_auth TokenSource
user-delegated, audience-bound bearer pattern in execution-core auth.rs (inference, browser-broker, data-plane, sandbox-manager) which already carries the zdr posture

capability registry CapabilityDetail.cost_class, risk_level and description for (b), and seed_tool_knowledge.sql agent_skills for steering tool choice
KnowledgePage WebSourcesPanel and PrivacyBadge for the Knowledge-page badge and undo
constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: promotion must remain a Quarry ingest that execution-core only triggers, and the document must land owner=user with private visibility in Data Plane, which owns the document and its ACL. ZDR must be a hard gate in maybe_promote (pass the run's resolved posture and refuse when active or unknown) because Quarry's service-token path trusts the caller's body flag. Execution-core has no database of its own, so a durable counter belongs in session-core or Data Plane. Promoted web text re-enters retrieval as context, so untrusted provenance must be preserved. Licensed premium sources stay behind integration-corev2 with per-call cost in cost-core.
approachAdjustment: Add the missing precondition first: a ZDR gate in maybe_promote, then a user-delegated ingest credential (only inference, browser-broker, data-plane and sandbox-manager delegated bearers exist; a Quarry-ingest audience or routing through the delegated Data Plane bearer would be new). Wire the chat-loop call site only after that, and prefer a citation-based signal over fetch counts. Split (b) out as a small separate item: add use_when and cost_hint to capability tool metadata (cost_class already exists) and generate the model-facing description from it instead of hand-editing prose in tool_loop.rs.
effortNote: Raised from M. (a) needs a ZDR gate (S), a user-delegated ingest credential across Auth Core, Quarry and execution-core (M), a durable counter in session-core (M), a citation signal (M) and a badge with undo plus web provenance on Data Plane documents (M); (b) alone is S.
verdictReason: Stub confirmed and risks are real, but the item omits the ZDR blocker and the missing delegated credential, and (a) and (b) have very different size; keep (a) as a low-priority arming checklist and (b) as a small quick win.

exactGap: Data Plane already has most of the approval half: wiki-store-go stores pages and versions, accepts agent proposals with source_refs (SubmitProposal, ReviewProposal), takes maintenance sweeps for stale, orphan and contradiction items, runs an operating-map proposal flow with human review in the Knowledge page, and data-orchestrator has a scheduled JobWikiRefresh; Model Plane exposes wiki_propose_edit and wiki_lint tools and POST /v1/wiki/proposals. What is missing is the generator and its feed: nothing reads session activity to draft pages (the refresh job only posts data-quality lint results, operating-map refresh is evidence-ref based, Dreaming writes personal agent_memory), SubmitProposal can only target an existing page, the BFF and Knowledge UI review only operating-map proposals, and staleness is lint and age based rather than source-change based. session-core already publishes RUN_COMPLETED events through its audit outbox (consumed by capability-core for skill learning) which a generator could subscribe to.
reuse: wiki-store-go proposals (page_id, proposed_content, source_refs, status) with ReviewProposal publishing a new version and emitting the wiki-published event
operating-map proposal, review route and KnowledgePage review UI as the human-approval surface to generalise
wiki_agent.rs propose_edit and lint tools and the model-gateway /v1/wiki/proposals routes
data-orchestrator JobWikiRefresh and the wiki maintenance sweep for stale and orphan marking
session-core learning_events RUN_COMPLETED outbox and the capability-core sessionreview consumer pattern (fetch transcript through an authorised read, then act) as the activity feed
Dreaming extractor (dream_extractor) for model-driven extraction with LLM-provenance links
constraints: Data Plane owns wiki storage and the page ACL (pages are scoped by org and workspace_id today), the Model Plane may only propose through the proposal route and humans accept, and session-core activity must reach Data Plane through a contract (the existing outbox events plus an authorised transcript read), never a cross-plane DB read. ZDR threads leave no durable transcript and wiki events are published with ZDR=false, so ZDR-origin content must be excluded at the source rather than filtered downstream. Personal memory (agent_memory user and thread scopes) must not enter a shared page without explicit opt-in, and Space access never widens a page's owner-plane ACL, so the source threads' audience must be intersected with the page audience.
approachAdjustment: Reuse the existing proposal-and-review path instead of designing a new approval path: add a create-page proposal kind (proposals can only edit an existing page today) and a generic wiki-proposal review view (only the operating map has one). Drive the generator from RUN_COMPLETED-style session-core events and start with Space or team scoped sources, not whole-org activity. Keep it a roadmap bet: its only external reference is documentation.
effortNote: XL stands for the generator, new-page proposals, a generic review UI and source-change staleness; the storage and approval half is already built, so it should not be re-sized upward, but it is also not a small extension.
verdictReason: The recommendation reads as greenfield but Data Plane already owns pages, versions, proposals, review and sweeps, and the Model Plane already proposes; reword to name the real delta (activity-to-page generator, new-page proposals, generic review UI) and keep it a late roadmap bet.
